situation: The first big right-hander of the lap. The road opens out, and there are three boost pads painted down the outside of it.

diagram.caption: The long way round is the painted way round.

answers.label: Swing out wide and drive over all three
answers.response: Three pads, three shoves forward, and you did not have to press a thing. Yes, you drove a few extra kart lengths to get out there — and they cost you a fraction of what the pads gave back. This is the whole habit: go the long way if the long way is boosted.

answers.label: Hug the inside — it is the shorter way round
answers.response: Shorter, and slower. That is the trap: the inside looks right, so it is what almost everybody does, and they hand back three boosts to save a couple of kart lengths. The distance is not what makes you fast here. The paint is.

answers.label: Stay in the middle and take whichever one you can reach
answers.response: The middle is the one line on this corner that gets you none of them. Pads are not that wide, and half-committing to the outside means arriving beside all three rather than on top of them. Pick the lane and go.

takeaway: Shorter is not the same as faster. If the long way round is painted, the long way round is the fast way.

situation: A long, lazy left-hander with one boost pad painted on it — tucked in tight against the inside kerb.

diagram.caption: One pad, and this time it is on the tight line.

answers.label: Tuck in tight and drive over it
answers.response: Right. Notice what just happened: last corner the answer was 'go wide', this one it is 'stay tight', and both answers came from the same place — looking at where the pads actually are. There is no rule to learn here. There is a track to learn.

answers.label: Out wide — that is where the pads live
answers.response: That was the last corner. Pads are painted wherever the people who built the track felt like painting them, and on this one they went on the inside. A rule you apply everywhere will be wrong somewhere; knowing the corner is never wrong.

answers.label: Ignore it — one pad is not worth changing your line for
answers.response: It is free speed sitting directly on your way, and you would have to steer around it to miss it. When the boost is on the tidy line, you get both, and that is the easiest point on the whole lap.

takeaway: There is no rule about which side the pads are on. There is only knowing this particular track.

situation: A long straight. There is a boost pad painted right up against the right-hand kerb, and you are cruising along the middle of the road quite happily.
prompt: What do you do about the pad?

diagram.caption: Half a road over. No corner for ages.

answers.label: Ease across and drive through it
answers.response: On a straight, moving sideways costs you almost nothing — you are still pointing the same way and still going the same speed. A shuffle across for a free boost is the best trade on the track, and it is available every single lap.

answers.label: Leave it — it is too close to the wall
answers.response: Your steering assist is switched on, which means the game actively stops you burying yourself in the barrier. Driving near a wall on a straight is one of the safest things you can do in this game, and there is a boost sitting there.

answers.label: Slow down a little so you can line it up properly
answers.response: Never this one. A pad is not a target you have to aim at — it is a great fat stripe of road you drive over. Lifting off to hit it means paying more speed than it gives back, which is the only way to lose money on a free boost.

takeaway: On a straight, a pad is always worth the shuffle across. It is never, ever worth slowing down for.

situation: Second lap. {rival} is a few kart lengths ahead of you, glued to the inside kerb like she always is. The pads are out on the wide side.

diagram.caption: Her line, and the painted one.

answers.label: Let her have the inside. Take the pads.
answers.response: Let her have it. She is driving the line that looks shortest, which is what everybody does when they have not looked the track up — and you get two boosts and a clear road for the trouble. This is the whole plan in one corner: she is quicker than you, and you know something she does not.

answers.label: Follow her — she wins, so she must know the way
answers.response: She wins because she reacts faster than you, not because she has studied anything. Copying her line means agreeing to race her at the one thing she is genuinely better at. Do not race her. Race the road.

answers.label: Sit in between so you can react to whatever she does
answers.response: Watching her is exactly the game you cannot win — she moves, you respond, and you are always half a second behind. You do not need to watch her at all. You need to be on the pads, which have not moved since 2014.

takeaway: You are not racing her line. You are racing the road, and you are the one who knows where the pads are.

situation: The pads on this corner sit past the bend, out of sight from where you are now. You only know they are there because you have driven this track before.
prompt: So how do you end up on the pads?

diagram.caption: This is the map, not the view. From where you are, all you can see is the corner.

answers.label: Start moving over to that side now, before you can see them
answers.response: That is it, and it is the reason this chapter exists. You are steering for something you cannot see, from memory, several seconds early — and arriving lined up while everyone else is still finding out. Preparation, quietly beating reaction.

answers.label: Wait until you can see them, then steer across
answers.response: By the time a pad appears on your screen you are practically level with it, and a kart does not move sideways that fast. Anything on a race track you have to react to, you have already missed. That is why the map matters more than the reflexes.

answers.label: Drive down the middle so you can go either way
answers.response: Keeping your options open is what you do on a road you do not know — and it is the right call there. But you already know this one. Once you know, hedging just means arriving in the wrong lane, politely.

takeaway: You cannot react to a boost pad. You can only remember it — which is exactly why {rival} drives past the ones you take.
